title: Federal Criminal Defense Lawyer Cost: CJA Rates and Fees (2026)
description: What federal criminal defense costs: who qualifies for a CJA lawyer, the 2026 CJA hourly rate, why federal cases cost more, and how private fees work.
h1: How much does a federal criminal defense lawyer cost?
summary: If you cannot afford a lawyer in federal court, the judge appoints a federal defender or a CJA panel lawyer at no cost or partial cost to you; there is no fixed income cutoff. CJA panel lawyers are paid $177 per hour in non-capital cases for work on or after January 1, 2026. Private federal defense is billed by phase or hourly against a retainer and cannot be contingent. Totals depend mainly on discovery volume, sentencing exposure and whether the case goes to trial.
body:
Two ways federal defense gets paid

If you are charged in federal court, your lawyer is paid in one of two ways. You either hire (retain) a private lawyer and pay the fee yourself, or the court appoints counsel under the Criminal Justice Act (CJA) because you cannot afford one. Appointed counsel is either a lawyer from a federal defender organization or a private lawyer from the court's CJA panel. There are 83 federal defender organizations serving 92 of the 94 federal judicial districts, and nationally they receive about 60% of CJA appointments, with panel lawyers taking the other 40% [1].

Who qualifies for a court-appointed federal lawyer

The CJA requires every district to have a plan for representing any person "financially unable to obtain adequate representation" [2]. There is no fixed income cutoff in the statute. The magistrate judge asks about your income, assets, debts and the likely cost of a lawyer for your type of case, usually on a sworn financial affidavit, and appoints counsel if satisfied you cannot afford one [2].

  • Partial ability to pay: if the court later finds you can pay part of the cost, it may end the appointment or order partial payment [2].
  • Funds found later: if money becomes available from you or on your behalf, the court can order it paid to appointed counsel or to the Treasury [2].
  • Coverage: appointed counsel represents you at every stage of the proceedings from your initial appearance onward [2].
Being "unable to afford" federal counsel is judged against what a federal case costs, not against a poverty line. People with a job and some savings sometimes qualify when the charges are complex. Answer the financial affidavit completely and truthfully.

What the government pays CJA panel lawyers

For work performed on or after January 1, 2026, CJA panel lawyers are paid $177 per hour in non-capital cases and up to $226 per hour in capital cases; the rate must cover the lawyer's office overhead too [1]. Compensation above case thresholds of $13,800 for a felony, $3,900 for a misdemeanor and $9,800 for an appeal needs approval from the chief judge of the circuit or a delegate [1].

Those rates are a useful benchmark when you read a private quote. Clio's 2025 data puts the average rate in its "criminal" category at $216 per hour and the all-lawyer average at $349 [3]. Experienced federal practitioners in major cities commonly charge more than either figure, so use these as a floor for comparison, not as a price list.

Why federal cases cost more than state cases

  • Volume of evidence. Federal investigations often run for months or years before charges, and discovery can include wiretaps, bank records, emails and phone extractions that take many hours to review.
  • The Sentencing Guidelines. Sentencing turns on detailed calculations (loss amount, drug quantity, role, criminal history), and challenging them is skilled, time-consuming work.
  • Mandatory minimums. In fiscal year 2025, 21% of federal cases carried a mandatory minimum penalty, and 68% of those were drug trafficking cases [6]. Arguments about whether a minimum applies or a safety valve is available add work.
  • Stakes. The average drug trafficking sentence in FY2025 was 87 months [7]; in theft and fraud cases, 75% of those sentenced went to prison and the median loss was $239,730 [8].
  • Experts and investigators. Forensic accountants, digital forensics and mitigation specialists are billed separately by retained counsel.

How private federal defense lawyers charge

Most retained federal lawyers use either a flat fee per phase (pre-indictment, through plea and sentencing, trial, appeal) or an hourly rate billed against a large advance retainer. Advance payments go into a client trust account and are withdrawn as the lawyer earns them [5]. Contingency fees are not allowed: ABA Model Rule 1.5(d)(2) prohibits a contingent fee for representing a defendant in a criminal case [4].

Example (illustrative, not a quote): a case that resolves by plea after 80 hours of lawyer time at the $349 national average costs 80 × $349 = $27,920. A case that goes to a two-week trial might need 400 hours: 400 × $349 = $139,600, before investigators or experts. The same 80 hours at the CJA non-capital rate would be paid at 80 × $177 = $14,160, which is above the $13,800 felony threshold and would need approval.

Questions to ask before you hire

  • How many federal cases have you handled in this district, and how many went to trial?
  • Is the fee flat or hourly, and exactly which phases does it cover? Is trial a separate fee?
  • Who pays for experts, investigators and discovery-review software?
  • If I run out of money mid-case, will you ask the court to be appointed under the CJA?
  • Will anyone else (a relative, an employer) be paying, and how will you protect my confidentiality?

Should you hire a lawyer or ask for appointed counsel?

Federal defenders and CJA panel lawyers handle federal cases every day and know the local judges and prosecutors. Hiring privately gets you a choice of lawyer and often a smaller caseload, but it only makes sense if you can pay for the whole case, including trial. If a private retainer would leave you unable to pay for experts or trial, ask the court about appointed counsel at your first appearance. If you received a target letter before any charges, contact a lawyer immediately; the federal defender's office can tell you whether it can help before an indictment.

See also white-collar crime lawyer cost, drug trafficking lawyer cost and criminal defense lawyer cost for state cases.

faq.q: Can I get a free lawyer in federal court?
faq.a: Yes, if the judge finds you are financially unable to obtain adequate representation. You fill out a financial affidavit, and if you qualify, a federal defender or CJA panel lawyer is appointed. The court can order partial payment if you can afford some of the cost.

faq.q: Are federal public defenders good lawyers?
faq.a: Federal defender offices practice only federal criminal law and handle cases in front of the same judges every day. Quality varies like anywhere, but appointed counsel is not a lesser category of lawyer. You can ask about their experience with your type of charge.

faq.q: Can my family pay my federal lawyer?
faq.a: Yes, a third party can pay, but you remain the client and the lawyer owes loyalty and confidentiality to you, not the payer. Be careful that the money is not proceeds of the alleged offense, because forfeitable assets can be recovered by the government.

faq.q: What does the CJA pay appointed lawyers?
faq.a: $177 per hour in non-capital cases and up to $226 per hour in capital cases for work on or after January 1, 2026, with case thresholds of $13,800 for felonies that require higher approval to exceed.
